en: The Vajra-Guhyasudvāra-Dhāraṇī Sūtra;
the translator’s name lost, appended to the Eastern Jin Records.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the World-Honored One was dwelling beneath the Bodhi tree together with his great disciples...
Śāriputra, Maudgalyāyana, and others were the leaders among them.
Furthermore, there were immeasurable great bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, whose names were as follows: Vajradhvaja Bodhisattva, and so forth.
Vajragarbha Bodhisattva, Maitreya Bodhisattva,
and the Great Beings of the Bhadrakalpa were also their leaders.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi,
empowered by the majestic spiritual authority of the Buddha, spoke these words:
"I pray only that the World-Honored One will analyze and expound the Dhāraṇī of the Gate of Goodness, which shall serve as a great illumination for the world."
It eradicates the malicious intent of enemies,
harmful influences, and evil associates. Whether they be devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas,
kumbhāṇḍas, humans, non-humans, or various great spirits and ghosts— [it subdues them all].
Those who consume the vital essence of others through left-handed paths and malevolent poisons,
and those enemies who employ deceit and flattery to watch for the shortcomings of others—
such as these have no place of refuge or protection.
The Tathāgata, through his great compassion, shall eliminate such matters as fear and anxiety,
establishing sentient beings upon the ground of purity, whether they are walking,
standing, sitting, lying down, or even in their dreams.
One should always protect [beings] so as not to let them fall into distress;
for the sake of this benefit, I now entreat you:
O Greatly Compassionate Tamer, please explain it for us.
Furthermore, one should protect those who follow the Mahāyāna,
causing their practice of firm merit and wisdom to be non-retrogressive,
and completely eliminating all enmity and harm so that their lives do not meet with untimely death.
At that time, after the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi had exhorted the Buddha,
he gazed up at the Honored One’s countenance with a mind full of longing remembrance.
Then the World-Honored One, the Great Compassionate Guide, [spoke].
He let out a great thunderous sound that pervaded the world,
praising the Bodhisattva Guhyakapada:
"Excellent, excellent, son of good family!"
"You are now truly a bodhisattva,
for you have posed such a question in order to bring peace and happiness to sentient beings."
"I shall now also, for the sake of all sentient beings,
proclaim this Dharani of the Good Gate.
At that time, Guhyapada was filled with unprecedented joy.
"I only pray that you will compassionately regard us and skillfully distinguish this for us.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Great Being, saying:
"Listen attentively, listen attentively, and reflect upon it well."
"I shall expound its meaning for you. Guhyapada replied, "So be it;
I accept your instruction," and immediately spoke this mantra:
Tadhe ta | Ūkṣu mukṣu | Mabinī | Madhinī | Panaraca | Inanhu | Hu hu li | Vata | Svāhā. At that time, the World-Honored One had finished reciting this consecration dhāraṇī.
Furthermore, he again proclaimed the words of the dhāraṇī:

*Tadyathā | vajre vajre vajradale vajrapaṭe vajrapiṭe vajramahī cakrāvarte cakradale dale dale bale mule cale culi huhuli pāke pinvale liliṇi luluzi cale culi mule maṇḍale*. This dhāraṇī is well able to eliminate all faults and evils.
It also eliminates all four hundred types of diseases and can further ensure that one's life does not end prematurely. Tadyathā:
Mātani-ga-garaṇi-muta-ni.
Saṃbhāramudānīnaśani (or Saṃbhāramudānīnaśanī)
naśani naśani bhaṭani
Cizhen dou cizhen dou bilili (Chi-chen tou chi-chen tou pi-li)
Mālikhatā nibali bali pṛthivī.
Dhṛtiviloṣalīśvarāṇīrāhave nīrāhave nandaśe.
Varamacalane-tara-vaṭṭi-dhiti-dharaseni.
Na-ma-he-sha-ba-ra-li-shi-pa-mo-hu-ni.
Pāpā yamamahunika rāvaḍi huśivaḍi.
Soma-paṭi soma-paravi svāhā tadyathā hara hara.
Hirīte mahāmopacā bhagavāṃ svāhā khaḍṭa ānuṇa ārija vani.
Kakadaṇī ātatahāṇi magavi.
Lohani hūsavaṭi hūsavaṭi.
Hili hili sataḥ satakiṇi sata pālañca sata vāyane.
*Svāhā sata-pāraṇa svāhā hili-dam svāhā.* At that time,
the World-Honored One spoke this Vajra Secret Gate Dharani.
If one desires to bring great benefit to humans and devas, causing them to forever leave behind suffering and hardship and always abide in peace and happiness,
those who uphold [this] in such a manner have already been taught by the Buddhas of the past.
The Buddhas of the future and the present shall likewise proclaim it together.
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi:
"Good son, out of great compassion and pity for all sentient beings, I now speak of it."
At that time, while the World-Honored One was speaking this dhāraṇī,
from his uṣṇīṣa— the invisible crown of his head— there issued forth the light of the mark of a Great Man, brilliant and resplendent,
illuminating immeasurable worlds throughout the ten directions.
At that time, all the Buddha-fields likewise became spontaneously transformed;
a radiant light surged forth, its wondrous color being rare and marvelous,
utterly extinguishing all darkness and obscurity.
At that time, the various classes of humans and devas from the ten directions all beheld this phenomenon and conceived a sense of wonder,
each thinking: "By what causes and conditions has this come about?"
Then this sign appeared, and light pervaded the world-systems.
At that time, the Buddhas addressed the assembly, saying:
"Sons of good family, listen attentively! There is a Buddha-world named Sahā."
The Buddha is named Śākyamuni Tathāgata.
Out of great compassion and pity for all sentient beings, and in order to bring them peace and happiness,
he has preached this *Dhāraṇī of the Gate of Goodness*.
At that time, having heard the Buddha’s teaching, the entire assembly, moved by the majestic power of Śākyamuni, raised their voices in unison to praise him, exclaiming:
"How marvelous! How excellent is Śākyamuni!
He has been able to give rise to great compassion for the Sahā world."
For the sake of bringing peace to devas and humans,
this dhāraṇī is taught; it is rare and signless, proclaimed by true wisdom.
We vow to joyfully and diligently practice this.
Having obtained this upholding, we shall likewise give rise to great compassion to teach and transform sentient beings.
The Buddhas praised him, saying, "Excellent, excellent, son of good family!
One who wishes to practice this Dharani of the Gate of Goodness should always chew wood and rinse with water at dawn."
Burn incense, scatter flowers, and recite with a concentrated mind, not allowing the senses to run wild among various objects. Why is this?
This dhāraṇī is that which has been upheld, taught, and used to transform beings by all the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
You all should keep this in mind and practice according to what has been taught:
let the five pungent herbs, wine, and meat never pass through your mouths;
let the pure conduct (brahmacarya) dwell in your hearts, and abandon all worldly affairs.
One should then recite it in a quiet place;
this can cause the practitioner to attain great merit and boundless wisdom.
Those who wish to practice the *dhāraṇī* of the Gate of Goodness should make a vow.
Do not let it be forgotten until you attain Buddhahood.
Recite it once every morning.
If you seek the fulfillment of present vows, do so for seven days and seven nights.
If one practices with diligence, there is nothing that will not be brought to fruition;
however, those who have committed grave offenses in the past cannot have them fully exhausted in this brief span of time.
All other karmas without exception shall be extinguished.
By cultivating all manner of wholesome deeds up to nirvana,
one will be able to fully attain the benefits of twenty meritorious qualities.
What are these twenty? They are:
long life, longevity, renown, the necessities of life, physical beauty, strength, freedom from illness, and courageous diligence.
The Buddhas protect and mind them, and their minds become harmonious and supple.
The devas protect and assist them as they vow to practice wholesome deeds.
They contemplate the profound meaning with diligent effort and without weariness.
With a radiant countenance and a joyful expression,

endowed with all marks of excellence, possessing fearless eloquence, and having fully perfected their roots of goodness— for these reasons, the World-Honored One has preached this Vajra Secret Profound and Sublime Gate Dharani.
You should recollect and practice with utmost sincerity. Why is this?
Because such a dhāraṇī is the most auspicious among all dhāraṇīs.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi addressed the Buddha,
saying: "World-Honored One,
I now take pity upon all sentient beings and shall protect them."
May they attain peace and happiness, may all sorrows and afflictions be removed, and may no evil find an opportunity.

Tadyathā | Niki niki | Jiji jiji | Bhabha bhabha | Ruru ruru | Sisi sisi | Kara kara kara kara | Hiri hiri hiri hiri | Phara phara phara phara | Mama mama mama mama | Hana hana hana hana | Dahaha dahaha dahaha dahaha | Banu agaye hitili svāhā. At that time, the World-Honored One praised Vajrapāṇi, saying:
Excellent, excellent, Great Being!
You are indeed able to proclaim this mantra of great majestic power, which protects all beings,
causing them all to attain peace and security and to increase their vital energy.
They shall not allow evil humans or non-humans to seize their vital essence or find an opportunity to harm them.
At that time, the Great Brahmā King and his retinue rose from their seats,
bared their right shoulders, and [proceeded].
With palms joined, he addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One,
I too now wish to rejoice and provide assistance to those who receive,
uphold, read, and recite the Śrīmahādevī Dhāraṇī."
May you increase the lifespan, physical strength, and vitality of sentient beings, removing their decline and ailments,
and ensuring that no one seeking to harm them finds an opportunity.
We pray only that the World-Honored One will bestow compassion and provide protection so that our wishes may be fulfilled.

Tadhe ta | Hiri | Miri | Cili | Svāhā | Varuṇa | Amā | Pūri | Svāhā | Varuṇa | Māpe | Vara | Kappa | Upasampadā | Svāhā. If there be any son or daughter of good family who wishes to practice this dhāraṇī:
Always at dawn, having purified oneself through washing and rinsing, one should recite this with a sincere mind.
At that time, Śakra Devānām Indra rose from his seat, bared one shoulder, joined his palms, and addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One..."
I now likewise desire to protect all sentient beings, so that no evil humans or non-humans may seize their vital essence or find an opportunity to harm them.
He then spoke these dhāraṇī phrases: Tadyathā: Viniparaṇi | Bhadramālaṃdhi | Cicciṭi | Gaurigandhārī | Bhramaraji | Ahamadantadhāraṇī | Bhramariṇī | Cakravākī | Śambharī | Śambharī | Svāhā.
When practicing this dharma of incantation,
one should always recite it with a sincere mind after having purified oneself at dawn.
At that time, the Four Heavenly Kings will immediately rise from their seats.
Exposing his right shoulder and joining his palms toward the Buddha,
he spoke these words: "We, too, wish to protect all sentient beings,
so that no evil humans or non-humans may harm them."
Those who spy for evil find their opportunity.
*Duòtiē tā* *Fúbī xiū fúbī* *Tóumó bōlí hālí* *Ālìyè bōluǒ zhǐ* *Xiān zhǐ nièmù zhǐ* *Mòqiélí duōdōu zhǐ dōu* *Svāhā*. This mantra should always be recited at dawn after one has purified oneself.
Recite this with a sincere heart.
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha raised his right hand and praised Brahmā, Śakra, and the Four Heavenly Kings, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, you all!
You have skillfully proclaimed the dhāraṇī phrases upheld by all Buddhas.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi.
Good son, if there are those who hear this *Sudvāra-dhāraṇī* and have no doubt or confusion in their minds,
and if they recite it with a sincere heart after purifying the three karmas at dawn, the merit they obtain will be beyond measure.
The Vajra Secret Gate of Skillful Means Dhāraṇī Sūtra (Vajraguhyamukhasupraviṣṭadhāraṇīsūtra)
